name: Dominican Republic
summary_text: The Dominican Republic demands real caution from trans visitors. Same-sex conduct between civilians is legal, but strikingly, Articles 210/260 still criminalise it for police and armed-forces members — challenged at the Constitutional Court in August 2024, revealing the institutional culture. There is no legal gender recognition, no anti-discrimination law covering SOGI (Brazil formally recommended one at the 2024 UPR), and documented violence against trans women is high, particularly affecting the most marginalised. Tourist zones (Punta Cana, Puerto Plata) are heavily insulated resort enclaves with international norms; Santo Domingo has a visible community and annual Pride caravan. Outside those bubbles, machista culture, police harassment of trans women (especially sex workers), and anti-Haitian dynamics that compound for dark-skinned trans people are documented.

sources.title: Dominican Republic: Court Reviews Laws Against Gay Sex | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: Human Rights Watch (Aug 2024): 'Dominican Republic: Court Reviews Laws Against Gay Sex' — constitutional court hearing challenges to penal-code provisions criminalising same-sex conduct.

sources.title: Brazil >> Dominican Republic, Recommendation, 46th Session, April 2024 | UPR Database
sources.claim_summary: UN UPR record (46th session, April 2024): Brazil recommended the Dominican Republic criminalise discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation and gender identity and ensure the right of trans and intersex persons to change name and gender in the civil registry - the recommendation was accepted.

sources.title: International Transgender Day of Visibility: A Conversation
sources.claim_summary: TIME/Amnesty International (March 2019): conversation between two trans activists for Transgender Day of Visibility - including Nairovi Castillo from the Dominican Republic sharing her story of trans life and activism there.
